title: Elliptical Polarization of Light
short_intro: Elliptical polarization is a state of optical polarization in which the electric field vector traces out an ellipse in any fixed plane intersecting, and normal to, the direction of propagation. It arises when two mutually orthogonal linearly polarized components of unequal amplitudes are superposed with a phase difference that is neither 0, pi, nor an integer multiple of pi.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Understanding the qualitative definitions of unpolarized, linearly, circularly, and elliptically polarized light; action of polarizers and quarter-wave plates; Malus's Law.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Rigorous derivation of the general equation of polarization ellipse from two orthogonal harmonic waves; conditions on amplitudes and phase differences for elliptical polarization; Stokes parameters and Jones calculus basics.

prerequisites: Superposition principle of orthogonal simple harmonic motions
Action of doubly refracting crystals (uniaxial crystals, ordinary and extraordinary rays)

concept_notes.heading: Fundamental Nature of Elliptical Polarization
bullets: The electric field vector E has two orthogonal components, E<sub>x</sub> and E<sub>y</sub>, oscillating in mutually perpendicular planes containing the propagation direction z.
The tip of the electric field vector traces out an ellipse as a function of time at any given point in space.
It represents the most general state of polarization for a monochromatic plane wave, encompassing linear and circular polarization as special cases.

concept_notes.heading: Conditions for Elliptical Polarization
bullets: The amplitudes of the two orthogonal components, E<sub>0x</sub> and E<sub>0y</sub>, must generally be unequal (though unequal amplitudes are not strictly required if the phase difference is not 0, pi/2, etc.).

The phase difference delta = phi<sub>y</sub> - phi<sub>x</sub> between the two components must be different from 0, pi, 2pi, etc. (which yield linear polarization) and different from +/- pi/2, +/- 3pi/2, etc. with equal amplitudes (which yield circular polarization).
The orientation of the ellipse's axes is inclined at an angle to the coordinate axes depending on the amplitude ratio and phase difference.

concept_notes.heading: Handedness or Chirality
bullets: Elliptical polarization can be either right-handed ( dextro-rotatory) or left-handed (laevo-rotatory).
Right-handed elliptical polarization corresponds to the electric vector rotating clockwise when viewed looking into the oncoming light beam.
Left-handed elliptical polarization corresponds to a counter-clockwise rotation of the electric vector.

concept_notes.heading: Production and Detection
bullets: Elliptically polarized light is produced when linearly polarized light is incident on a quarter-wave plate (or any arbitrary retarder) with its vibration azimuth oriented at an angle other than 0, pi/2, or multiples of pi/4 relative to the optic axis.
It can be detected using a combination of a quarter-wave plate and an analyzer (polarizer), where rotation of the analyzer yields varying intensity without ever reaching complete extinction.
The minimum and maximum transmitted intensities through a rotating analyzer correspond to the squares of the semi-minor and semi-major axes of the polarization ellipse.

derivations.title: Derivation of the General Polarization Ellipse
derivations.conditions: Two orthogonal harmonic waves propagating along the z-axis with arbitrary amplitudes and phase difference delta.
steps: Write the orthogonal electric field components: E_x = E_{0x} \cos(\omega t - kz) and E_y = E_{0y} \cos(\omega t - kz + \delta).
Expand the second equation using trigonometric identity: E_y / E_{0y} = \cos(\omega t - kz)\cos\delta - \sin(\omega t - kz)\sin\delta.
Express cos(omega t - kz) as E_x / E_{0x} and sin(omega t - kz) as \sqrt{1 - (E_x / E_{0x})^2}.

Substitute these into the expanded E_y equation, isolate the radical term, square both sides, and rearrange into the standard quadratic form: \frac{E_x^2}{E_{0x}^2} + \frac{E_y^2}{E_{0y}^2} - 2\frac{E_x E_y}{E_{0x} E_{0y}}\cos\delta = \sin^2\delta.
derivations.result: The general equation of an ellipse rotated relative to the coordinate axes: \frac{E_x^2}{E_{0x}^2} + \frac{E_y^2}{E_{0y}^2} - 2\frac{E_x E_y}{E_{0x} E_{0y}}\cos\delta = \sin^2\delta

derivations.title: Orientation Angle of the Polarization Ellipse
derivations.conditions: Relating the angle psi between the major axis of the ellipse and the x-axis.
steps: Using the general ellipse equation, the orientation angle psi of the major axis with the x-axis is given by the coordinate transformation relation.
Apply the condition for rotation of axes to eliminate the cross-term E_x E_y.
Obtain the relation involving the amplitudes E_{0x}, E_{0y} and the phase difference delta.

solved_numericals.question: A beam of light has orthogonal electric field components given by E_x = 3 \cos(\omega t) and E_y = 4 \cos(\omega t + \pi/2). Describe the state of polarization.
solution_steps: Identify the amplitudes: E_{0x} = 3 and E_{0y} = 4.
Since the phase difference is \pi/2 and amplitudes are unequal (3 != 4), the condition corresponds to elliptical polarization with axes parallel to the coordinate axes.
solved_numericals.answer: Elliptically polarized light with semi-axes 3 and 4 parallel to the coordinate axes.

solved_numericals.question: For an elliptically polarized light wave, the orthogonal amplitudes are E_{0x} = 2 V/m and E_{0y} = 3 V/m, and the phase difference is delta = \pi/3. Find the constant term representing sin^2(delta) in the ellipse equation and write the ellipse equation.
solution_steps: Substitute E_{0x} = 2, E_{0y} = 3, and \cos(\pi/3) = 1/2 into the general ellipse equation.
The cross-term coefficient is 2(E_x E_y / (2 \times 3)) \cos(\pi/3) = (E_x E_y / 3) \times (1/2) = E_x E_y / 6.
Substitute into the standard formula: \frac{E_x^2}{4} + \frac{E_y^2}{9} - \frac{E_x E_y}{3} = \frac{3}{4}.

solved_numericals.question: An elliptically polarized light beam passing through a rotating analyzer shows a maximum intensity of 9 units and a minimum intensity of 1 unit. Calculate the ratio of the semi-major axis to the semi-minor axis (a/b) of the polarization ellipse.
solution_steps: Recall that maximum intensity is proportional to the square of the semi-major axis: I_{max} = k a^2.
Recall that minimum intensity is proportional to the square of the semi-minor axis: I_{min} = k b^2.
Take the ratio: I_{max} / I_{min} = a^2 / b^2.
Substitute values: 9 / 1 = a^2 / b^2, which gives a / b = \sqrt{9/1} = 3.
solved_numericals.answer: Ratio of semi-major to semi-minor axis (a/b) = 3:1

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumes monochromatic light waves of a single fixed frequency.
Assumes a homogeneous, non-magnetic, and isotropic medium for propagation after polarization.
Limitations apply when dealing with polychromatic light where polarization states vary across frequencies, requiring Stokes parameter integration.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Elliptical polarization requires equal amplitudes for the orthogonal electric field components.
common_misconceptions.correct: Elliptical polarization generally occurs with unequal amplitudes; equal amplitudes with a pi/2 phase difference result in circular polarization.
common_misconceptions.why: Circular polarization is just a symmetric special case of elliptical polarization where a = b.

common_misconceptions.wrong: When elliptically polarized light passes through an analyzer, the minimum intensity is always zero.
common_misconceptions.correct: The minimum intensity is zero only for linearly polarized light.
common_misconceptions.why: For elliptical polarization, the electric vector never vanishes; it only shrinks to the semi-minor axis, yielding a non-zero minimum intensity.

quick_revision: Elliptical polarization is produced by the superposition of two orthogonal linear vibrations with unequal amplitudes and a phase difference other than integral multiples of pi.
Orthogonal X-Component of Electric Field: E_x(z,t) = E_{0x} \cos(\omega t - kz)
Orthogonal Y-Component of Electric Field: E_y(z,t) = E_{0y} \cos(\omega t - kz + \delta)
